The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen. I wandered through the narrow streets, looking at the house fronts with their cracked and uneven plaster. In some places the stones had fallen and there were gaps in the walls where the brick showed through. The pavement was wet with recent rain, and a steady drip from the eaves fell with monotonous regularity into the puddles. I walked without direction, save for the general sense of moving toward the river.
